neighbours.label: a span of time remaining or allotted to someone ('six months left', 'had twelve months to'), not other quantities left or time merely elapsed
fire: According to her surgeon, my aunt had four months left when the new treatment finally arrived.
They led by a single goal with barely eight minutes left on the clock.
The surveyors had eighteen months to complete the whole of the northern route.
He knows he has maybe two years left, and he intends to spend them by the sea.
After the ruling, the company has nine months to repay all of its customers.
Applicants now have only three weeks left to send in the forms.
Once diagnosed, the old fisherman was given six weeks to live by his doctors.
With seven minutes remaining in the final, the visitors finally scored from a corner.
quiet: According to her neighbour, my aunt had four cats left when the new landlord finally arrived.
They ran out of fuel with barely eight litres left in the tank.
The surveyors walked eighteen kilometres over the whole of the northern route.
He knows he has maybe two biscuits left, and he intends to eat them by the sea.
After the merger, the company has nine offices across all of its regions.
The festival ran for three weeks and drew crowds from the nearby towns.
Once restored, the old fishing boat was sailed for six weeks by its owners.
The war dragged on for seven years before the two sides finally signed a truce.

notes: Card mixes ' spend', ' takes', ' minutes', ' months'. Its + pole is ' amount' of time and promotes ' time'. Probes: 'six months left' 0.65, 'five minutes left' 0.49, 'twelve months to' 0.25; apples or miles left and 'lasted twelve months' under 0.02. Bare 'spend' probed low, so the spend/takes peaks are likely not covered.
